item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hiya, I go by Hypastryx! I joined the site because I utterly love creative writing (Have been doing so for 6 years now) and SCP as a concept in and of itself always fascinated me. I *hope* as opposed to plan, to create one or more SCPs that are an interesting read, while also providing a more psychological side to the creatures/humanoids themselves that I create. I also love the atmosphere provided by a community with a set up like this, and even if my first ones divebomb I'm just thrilled to be here!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey DashDotBlank, and welcome to the site! Always great to welcome a long time fan to the ranks of members here. I like your attitude towards all this, and it's definitely a process to get an idea critiqued and reviewed before being able to even get to the drafting phase. With those kind of themes, I think you'll fit in just fine. As well as good taste in games, enjoy the gaming. Take your time and get acquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5552

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

For posting ideas, make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!

item.content:encoded:
Hello. I'm PoeticStanza. I'm kinda a lurker on the site, but I do occasionally like to make minor edits for grammar and syntaxes. I may end up contributing a bit to certain experiment logs, namely some of the more creative experiments like 914, 261, and 1459. I don't currently have any large ambitions to write articles but I do look forward to enjoying all the site has to offer.

Why I joined: I mostly want the chance to read articles unimpeded and maybe add to some of the more community-driven experiments.

What I want to do: mostly lurk and vote, but participate in interesting projects

Hobbies/Interests: I've been a creative writer for a while, and I'm very passionate about music.

What keeps me up at night: bees and clowns (particularly Bobble). There's also my everyday existential crises and the idea that nothing I do in life will ever matter in the long run.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, fellow members. I am a freelance horror writer currently going to school at Full Sail U for creative writing. I was always a fan of the SCP genre of things, since long before I started writing. You could say, among other things, it somewhat inspired me to my own writing. And now that I am confident enough in my particular form of horror, I have decided to present myself among you all and begin the process of adding my own work to this glorious work of art we know as the SCP Foundation.

Personally, I have a deep and longing fascination with the horrors of the mind. This sprouted from an experiment I performed on myself with lucidity and the effects of uncontrolled experimentation. You see, the lucid state in which I brought upon myself didn't exactly stop when I wanted it to. It became abundantly clear to me that no matter what I did, I would eventually be conscious when I went to sleep. In this time spent in a lucid state, I began to feel as if I was being followed by something I had not created there. Or perhaps someone I had created unknowingly. Eventually, the method I had used to gain lucidity wore and with it, the state.

Nevertheless, I lay awake at night knowing that he… or it… is still in there somewhere.

Sorry if that was a little too much.
